commit_message:
SyncTestBackend and CompositeMiddleware use the shared worker body and hook runner (#19)

* SyncTestBackend and CompositeMiddleware use the shared worker body and hook runner (#15)

- SyncTestBackend.launch runs _compute_and_record, so the test double follows
  the real backends' contract: BaseException recorded then re-raised, one
  release hook per job, error stored as the exception (was str; see #18).
- InMemoryStore stamps completed_at on a terminal write, as FileSystemStore
  does, so results keep their duration.
- CompositeMiddleware drives its children through _call_hooks: one failing
  child no longer stops the rest.
- ComputationBackend._run_middleware_* had no caller left: deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes: real durations, one completion stamp, public helper names (#15)

- compute_and_record takes created_at before the call, so a result's
  duration is the run's (it was ~0 on every backend).
- ComputationResult stamps completed_at on a terminal result when made; the
  two stores' copies of that stamp are gone.
- _compute_and_record / _call_hooks are used across modules: renamed
  compute_and_record / call_hooks.
- error and on_error are annotated BaseException; SyncTestBackend's
  docstring says what it records.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-review fixes: keep TTL from created_at; stable completion time on read (#15)

- Revert created_at=start: TTL expiry counts from created_at, so a job longer
  than its TTL was expired the moment it finished. The duration question
  goes to #20.
- FileSystemStore._deserialize restores the stored completed_at instead of
  letting __post_init__ stamp the read time.
- on_error overrides are annotated BaseException like the protocol.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------
